This way each ebuild doesn't need to manually construct the path. Also always use `--release` when building the code. The cros-debug flag is only going to control whether or not we enable debug assertions. cros-rust: Clean up env var handling Clean up environment variable handling so that they are all exported in the src_configure function rather than being exported in an ad hoc way all over the eclass. Packages that use this eclass are now always built with debuginfo=2, optlevel=3, and link-time optimization. Integer overflow checks are also enabled by default as they should have a trivial performance impact on most binaries. Packages that are drastically affected by the overflow checks can set CROS_RUST_OVERFLOW_CHECKS=0 to disable this option. Overflow checks and debug assertions are still always enabled when the cros-debug USE flag is set. Also clean up the rustflag handling and export rustflags in src_configure. This should make it possible to build binaries and run tests with sanitizers enabled without restricting them to fuzzers. BUG=chromium:910832,chromium:910831 TEST=emerge various rust packages with different combinations of USE flags and trybots Change-Id: I212adfe52fd7f7f2cfd95c00e326e96c8e369b00 Signed-off-by: Chirantan Ekbote <chirantan@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1385085 Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

motion_sense: send ODR events to the AP This commits enables the EC to send a motion sense event to the AP when a sensor's ODR is changed. This is done in a way that is backwards compatible on the AP side, in order to enable previous kernels to continue to work (albeit at a loss of new functionality) with up-to-date ECs. Since clients are not required to use a FLUSH when changing ODR, it is possible for the sensor ring to get in a state where it is spreading based on out-of-date delay information, which we observed leading to spreading of overly large intervals, and thus too far into the future. This patch ameliorates that by causing an ODR change to implicitly flush the batching history. BUG=b:123700100 TEST=run CTS sensor tests, observe the sensor ring not spreading too far into the future due to a period change BRANCH=bobba Change-Id: I5a881e9fc5ddb1dbe6690c455d43dc20bffe889a Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1450288 Commit-Ready: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Tested-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: cros_ec: use ODR events to clear the spreading history This uses the ODR flag introduced in CL:1450288 to clear the last batch data used by the spreading algorithm. The spreading code relies on accurately measuring the effective interval between batches of samples. An ODR change means that the previous batches may no longer represent the behavior of the EC. If an ODR change is immediately followed by a batch, the AP will attempt to spread based on the previous interval, which can easily lead to "spreading into the future", leading to subsequent timestamp mismatch errors. This patch solves that problem by having ODR events be breaking points for the spreading code. The tradeoff is that this can cause samples to be lost immediately after an ODR change. This problem can't effectively be solved without either: - storing those samples in a side queue and spreading them once updated information becomes available to do so; - communicating the ODR to the AP as part of the ODR event. BUG=b:123700100 TEST=running with CL:1450791, observe the ring not using stale batch information CQ-DEPEND=CL:1450288 Change-Id: Ic73d1bf0e7f659210052c56fe8d265f82f7f4b58 Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1450743 Commit-Ready: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Tested-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org>

gerrit: provide option to suppress emails on some operations When cherry picking large stacks of patches into branches, gerrit generates emails on every operation along the way: ready, verify, review, This results in tons of noise of which the recipients usually do not care about. This patch adds a command line option which allows to suppress sending emails on ready, review, trybotready, and verify gerrit operations. BUG=none TEST=using the new command line option modified the 'verified' flag of an existing gerit patch. Observed that emails are not generated when --ne s passed in as a command line argument, and are generated in case --ne is not present. Reland "minigbm: define GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER" It seems like the problem was that the GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_PLANAR was redifened to 0x5505 from 0x5504. And GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER was added as 0x5504, which lead to crashes. In order to minimize risks, do it other way round - leave GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_PLANAR as 0x5504 and add GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER as 0x5505. Once all the call sites are changed to use GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER, remove GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_PLANAR and make GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER to be 0x5505. Original change's description: > minigbm: define GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER > > This CL aligns the minigbm more with the upstream GBM > by defining GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER and using > gbm_import_fd_modifier_data instead. > > That is, the main difference between the old > gbm_import_fd_planar_data one and the new one is > the format_modifiers variable. In the upstream > GBM, it's a single variable. In the minigbm, it is > an array. > > As we know there are no cases when modifiers would > be different for each plane. Thus, it's safe to eliminate > that and adapt more to the upstream. > > Change-Id: Iaae062ef1fe9fc9ab0ead09c5f4bfa91d2db67c3 > Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1360771 > Commit-Ready: Maksim Sisov <msisov@igalia.com> > Tested-by: Maksim Sisov <msisov@igalia.com> > Reviewed-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Change-Id: I1617de54914734c903cb05e1694cc782a7bb171a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1454658 Commit-Ready: Maksim Sisov <msisov@igalia.com> Tested-by: Maksim Sisov <msisov@igalia.com> Tested-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org>

mt8173: remove LDFLAG --fix-cortex-a53-843419 This flag was added to enable an errata for the little core (A53) on MT8173 chips. However, this errata only affects arm64 linking, not arm32. The entire userspace for the Chromium OS mt8173 build is actually arm32, only the kernel is built for arm64. Since the kernel handles this flag itself, via the CONFIG_ARM64_ERRATUM_843419 KConfig option, this LDFLAG need not be set in the chipset overlay. bluetooth: Convert all async D-Bus exporting to sync. BlueZ D-Bus API is very sensitive to timing of D-Bus events. For example 1. Export an interface (emits an InterfacesAdded signal) 2. Set a value to a property (emits a PropertiesChanged signal) Action 2 might signify to client that it's ready to consume the interface exported by action 1. Therefore it's important to guarantee that the actions are executed in order. A simple way to achieve this by having all D-Bus signals triggered synchronously (directly sent) or asynchronously (queued to be sent later), but not a combination of both. All synchronous is chosen since it's simpler than all asynchronous and sending D-Bus messages doesn't block anyway. This CL changes all async D-Bus exporting operations to sync.
